films.title: Two Days In Dallas
films.writer: Jim Kempner, Will Kempner, Matt Kempner
films.logline: A father and son go to Dallas for the 60th anniversary of the JFK assassination.
films.review: Will Kempner brings authentic vision to Two Days In Dallas that demonstrates strong command of the medium, through carefully composed frames, while orchestrating visual motifs. Will Kempner offers a film of quiet determination.

films.title: the hypnosis movie
films.review: eda dalaman's vision in the hynosis movie crystallizes as a metaphoric statement that deepens structural resonance, with remarkable visual sophistication, through choices that emphasize stability. A film that reflects careful consideration.

films.title: Big Red's Theme
films.logline: From the album "Songs for the Moon" by The Fascinating Chimera Project, out on Misery Mother Records on March 28 2025
films.directorStatement: We wrote this song as a theme song for a neighborhood cat named Big Red, who we used to see out and about on warm days, and who would occasionally come right up to our porch for a visit and some pets.
films.review: Director Vanessa Castro approaches animation with fresh eyes in Big Red's Theme while embracing genre conventions, with remarkable visual sophistication, while maintaining a consistent tone. A film that prioritizes atmosphere over immediacy.

films.title: On My Days Off
films.review: Noah Engel renders On My Days Off as a formally attentive work while creating genuine moments of connection, through assured performances, with disciplined tonal modulation. The film establishes Noah Engel as a name to remember.

films.title: Submarine Story
films.logline: A submarine scientist returns to the surface
films.review: Mischa Aletta situates Submarine Story within systemic critique that feels fresh and original, through strategically layered editing, through natural performances. This confirms Mischa Aletta's commitment to politically engaged cinema.

films.title: TRAVELING MAN
films.review: Director Graham Mason crafts something special with TRAVELING MAN while deepening emotional complexity, through controlled shifts in perspective, that favors subtlety over impact. Graham Mason brings discipline to the material.

films.title: Bronze Dog
films.logline: A guy tries to get over a breakup by making a documentary about it.
films.directorStatement: I was in my feelings about a girlie.
films.cast: Mike Bernieri, Edy Modica, Alex Bliss
films.review: Bronze Dog marks an impressive comedy entry from I was in my feelings about a girlie while exploring complex themes with subtlety, through thoughtful production design. with memorable visual moments. A strong work that demonstrates considerable skill.

films.title: Calabasas 1/26/20
films.logline: A dense fog in the San Fernando Valley disupts a meeting of UFO hunters and causes unexpected tragedy in the nearby mountains.
films.review: Xavier Rotnofsky foregrounds labor conditions in Calabasas 1/26/20 through natural performances, that gestures toward larger themes, through repetition of familiar beats. Xavier Rotnofsky has created something genuinely memorable.

films.title: Swimming in Your Skin Again
films.producer: Jason Fitzroy Jeffers, Keisha Rae Witherspoon, Jonathan David Kane
films.logline: An experimental short based on the work of musician and producer Norvis Jr
films.review: Swimming in Your Skin Again represents a careful effort from Terence Nance through deliberate visual pacing, with a noticeably restrained energy, with deliberate compositional framing. This affirms Terence Nance's authority over cinematic form.
